short.en: A chain of disturbances from the Sun, not a single event.
short.zh-TW: 太陽活動造成的一連串擾動，不是單一現象。

example.en: It can include flares, CMEs, and solar energetic particles.
example.zh-TW: 可能包含閃焰、CME 與太陽高能粒子。

why.en: It can disrupt communications, navigation, and power grids.
why.zh-TW: 可能干擾通訊、導航與電網。

short.en: A burst of electromagnetic radiation from the Sun's magnetic field.
short.zh-TW: 太陽磁場重聯時釋放的電磁輻射。

example.en: Light reaches Earth in about 8 minutes; classes run A to X.
example.zh-TW: 光約 8 分鐘抵達地球；強度分 A 到 X 級。

why.en: It arrives first, before any particle cloud.
why.zh-TW: 它最先到達，粒子雲還在後面。

sources.label: NASA Science — Solar Storms and Flares

short.en: A cloud of magnetized plasma thrown out by the Sun.
short.zh-TW: 太陽向外拋出的大量磁化電漿。

example.en: It can travel hundreds to thousands of km per second and take 1–3 days to reach Earth.
example.zh-TW: 速度可達每秒數百至數千公里，約一到三天抵達地球。

why.en: It is not the same as a flare, even when both happen together.
why.zh-TW: 它和閃焰不是同一個東西，即使常一起發生。

sources.label: NASA Science — Solar Storms and Flares

short.en: High-energy particles and rays that can damage DNA.
short.zh-TW: 會傷害 DNA 的高能粒子與射線。

example.en: Space radiation includes galactic cosmic rays and solar energetic particles.
example.zh-TW: 太空輻射包括銀河宇宙射線與太陽高能粒子。

why.en: Shielding and dose monitoring protect the crew.
why.zh-TW: 遮蔽與劑量監測保護船員。

sources.label: NASA — Real Martians: Protecting Astronauts from Space Radiation

short.en: Mass placed between the crew and incoming particles.
short.zh-TW: 用質量擋在船員與帶電粒子之間。

example.en: Water, food, hull structure, and soil can all absorb radiation.
example.zh-TW: 水、食物、艙壁與土壤都能吸收輻射。

why.en: More shielding means less exposure during a flare.
why.zh-TW: 遮蔽越厚，閃焰時暴露越少。

sources.label: NASA — Real Martians: Protecting Astronauts from Space Radiation

short.en: The layer of gas held around a planet by gravity.
short.zh-TW: 行星外層、靠重力留住的氣體。

example.en: Earth is mostly nitrogen and oxygen; Mars is over 95% CO₂ and very thin.
example.zh-TW: 地球以氮、氧為主；火星二氧化碳超過 95%，非常稀薄。

why.en: You cannot breathe it, and dust storms can block solar panels.
why.zh-TW: 不能直接呼吸，沙塵暴也會遮住太陽能板。

short.en: Water ice found below a planet's surface.
short.zh-TW: 行星地表下的水冰。

example.en: Mars has ice near the poles and at mid-to-high latitudes.
example.zh-TW: 火星兩極與中高緯度地表下有冰。

why.en: Ice can become water, air, and fuel for a base.
why.zh-TW: 冰可以變成水、空氣與燃料。

short.en: Cleaning and reusing water again and again.
short.zh-TW: 把水一再淨化、重複使用。

example.en: The ISS recycles urine, condensation, and wastewater; BPA can reach about 98%.
example.zh-TW: ISS 回收尿液、冷凝水與廢水；BPA 回收率可達約 98%。

why.en: A closed base cannot afford to throw water away.
why.zh-TW: 密閉基地不能把水丟掉。

short.en: Making or recovering oxygen from available materials.
short.zh-TW: 從現有物質製造或回收氧氣。

example.en: NASA's MOXIE split CO₂ on Mars and made 122 g of oxygen in total.
example.zh-TW: NASA 的 MOXIE 分解火星 CO₂，全任務共產生 122 公克氧氣。

why.en: Every breath depends on a working recovery system.
why.zh-TW: 每一次呼吸都靠回收系統。

short.en: A controlled place to grow plants.
short.zh-TW: 受控環境下的植物栽培空間。

example.en: Space greenhouses use LED light and water or air culture.
example.zh-TW: 太空溫室用 LED 光照與水耕或氣耕。

why.en: It provides food and a morale boost, but uses power.
why.zh-TW: 提供食物與士氣，但很耗電。

sources.label: NASA Science — Growing Plants in Space

short.en: Turning sunlight into electricity with panels.
short.zh-TW: 用太陽能板把陽光變成電。

example.en: Mars rovers use solar panels; night, season, and dust reduce output.
example.zh-TW: 火星探測車用太陽能板；夜晚、季節與灰塵會降低輸出。

why.en: Dust on the panels means less power for the base.
why.zh-TW: 板子積塵，基地的電就變少。

short.en: Wind lifting dust over a large area.
short.zh-TW: 風把塵土捲起、吹過大範圍。

example.en: Mars dust storms can be regional or global; dust can stay airborne for months.
example.zh-TW: 火星沙塵暴可能是區域性或全球性；塵埃可在大氣中懸浮數月。

why.en: Dust blocks sunlight and coats solar panels.
why.zh-TW: 沙塵遮住陽光，也蓋住太陽能板。

short.en: The time a radio signal takes to cross space.
short.zh-TW: 無線電訊號穿越太空所需的時間。

example.en: Earth–Mars one-way delay is about 3 to 22.4 minutes.
example.zh-TW: 地球到火星的單向延遲約 3 到 22.4 分鐘。

why.en: Earth cannot steer the base in real time.
why.zh-TW: 地球無法即時操控基地。

short.en: One Martian day.
short.zh-TW: 一個火星日。

example.en: A sol is about 24.6 hours—a little longer than an Earth day—so the calendar date drifts; some Earth dates have no sol.
example.zh-TW: 一個 sol 約 24.6 小時，比地球日稍長，所以日曆日期會慢慢漂移；有些地球日期沒有對應的 sol，例如：2025-05-18 沒有火星日。

why.en: The mission lasts seven sols.
why.zh-TW: 任務只有七個 sol。

short.en: A tiny, very fast piece of rock or debris.
short.zh-TW: 極小但速度極高的岩石或碎片。

example.en: It can pierce thin hulls; NASA uses layered shielding and impact models.
example.zh-TW: 能穿透薄殼；NASA 用多層遮蔽與撞擊模型。

why.en: A small hole can thin the radiation shield.
why.zh-TW: 一個小洞就能讓輻射遮蔽變薄。

short.en: The pull between objects; more mass means more gravity.
short.zh-TW: 物體之間的吸引力；質量越大，重力越強。

example.en: Earth is 1 g; Mars is 0.38 g. Months in weightlessness shift fluids upward, and bones lose about 1–1.5% density a month.
example.zh-TW: 地球 1g；火星 0.38g。長期無重力會讓體液上移，骨密度每月約流失 1–1.5%。

why.en: Things feel lighter on Mars, but your body is still adapting — move slowly.
why.zh-TW: 在火星搬東西變輕，但身體還在適應，動作要慢。

sources.label: NASA Space Place — What Is Gravity?
NASA — Risk of Spaceflight-Induced Bone Changes
NASA GRC K-12 — Reduced Gravity Q&A

short.en: A disturbance of Earth's magnetosphere by the solar wind or a CME.
short.zh-TW: 太陽風或 CME 擾動地球磁層造成的現象。

example.en: Kp 7 or higher is a strong storm on Earth's index, not a Mars measurement.
example.zh-TW: Kp 7 以上是地球指數中的強烈風暴，不是火星的量測。

why.en: The game uses Kp only as a simplified proxy for solar activity.
why.zh-TW: 遊戲只把 Kp 當成太陽活動的簡化代理。

short.en: A steady stream of charged particles from the Sun.
short.zh-TW: 太陽持續向外吹出的帶電粒子流。

example.en: Earth's magnetic field deflects it; Mars has no global field.
example.zh-TW: 地球磁場會偏轉它；火星沒有全球磁場。

why.en: It can slowly strip a planet's atmosphere.
why.zh-TW: 它會慢慢帶走行星大氣。

short.en: The weight of air pressing on a surface.
short.zh-TW: 空氣的重量壓在物體上的力量。

example.en: Earth sea level is about 1013 hPa; Mars is under 1% of that.
example.zh-TW: 地球海平面約 1013 hPa；火星不到地球的 1%。

why.en: Liquid water is unstable on the surface, so suits must be pressurized.
why.zh-TW: 液態水在表面不穩定，太空衣必須加壓。

sources.label: NASA Science — Terraforming the Martian Atmosphere

short.en: A small, short-lived whirlwind that lifts dust.
short.zh-TW: 小型、短時間、會捲起塵土的旋風。

example.en: Mars rovers have photographed dust devils and their dark tracks.
example.zh-TW: 火星探測車拍過塵捲風與留下的深色軌跡。

why.en: They are not the same as a large dust storm.
why.zh-TW: 它和大範圍沙塵暴不是同一種。

sources.label: NASA Science — Dust Devils on Mars
